prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single “official” service that tells you whether general-purpose LLMs (like ChatGPT) will recommend your business. Instead use two things together:
- a listings/knowledge-management service to make sure authoritative sources have correct, prominent info about your business (so AI systems that draw on web/search/knowledge graphs are more likely to surface you), and
- regular testing across the major AI chat engines to see whether and how they recommend you.

Recommended services and tools
- Yext — best single product for pushing correct facts across many directories, maps and knowledge providers (helps the knowledge graph signals many assistants/search engines use).
- Google Business Profile (free) — essential. Google is a major source for assistants and for generative models’ underlying web signals.
- Bing Places + Apple Maps + Yelp — claim and optimize these (Bing influences Bing Chat; Apple influences Siri/Maps).
- Local SEO monitoring / rank tracking: BrightLocal, Whitespark, Moz Local, Semrush Local — track local-pack visibility and citations.
- Reputation/mention monitoring: Brand24, Mention, Google Alerts — track web mentions that feed model training data.

How to test directly whether AI engines recommend you
1. Manual testing: Ask the big chatbots directly:
   - ChatGPT (GPT-4/4o) — explicitly ask for local recommendations: “Recommend a [your business type] in [city/zip].” If using ChatGPT Plus or Enterprise, ask follow-ups and ask it to cite sources.
   - Google Bard / Google’s Gemini-powered chat
   - Bing Chat (Microsoft) — tends to cite web sources
   - Anthropic Claude
   - Siri/Google Assistant (voice queries on devices)
2. Use consistent prompts and log results so you can compare over time. Example prompts:
   - “Recommend a family-friendly Italian restaurant within 2 miles of [address/zip]. Why did you pick it? Cite sources.”
   - “List the top three plumbers in [city] and give the phone number and one review source for each.”
3. Automated testing (advanced): write scripts that call the models’ APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic) with your test prompts on a schedule so you can monitor changes over time.
4. Ask for sources: when a model lists a business, ask “Where did you get that?” Models that can browse/cite will point to websites or knowledge panels.

Why this approach works
- Most LLMs don’t have a single “business recommendation directory” you can opt into. They synthesize from web pages, knowledge graphs, reviews and directories. If your business is present and authoritative in those sources (GMB, Yelp, major publications, schema markup on your site), it’s far more likely to be recommended.
- Managing your facts (via Yext or manually) plus building reviews and citations is the most reliable way to influence AI recommendations.

Practical checklist (quick)
- Claim & optimize Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp, Apple Maps.
- Use schema.org LocalBusiness markup on your website.
- Get consistent NAP (name/address/phone) across directories.
- Collect good reviews and respond to them.
- Use Yext / Moz Local /BrightLocal to distribute and monitor listings.
- Periodically test ChatGPT, Bard, Bing Chat, Claude with the prompts above and log results.

If you want, tell me your business type and city and I’ll:
- suggest 2–3 tailored test prompts you can use, and
- recommend which combination of listing and monitoring services would give the best ROI for your situation.
